summary: Iter 56f Cloudinary migration verified end-to-end on the preview env. New backend test file /app/backend/tests/test_iter56f_cloudinary.py runs 13 pytest cases — ALL 13 PASS (100%). Verified BE#1 PNG upload → https://res.cloudinary.com/dwocjyvys/image/upload/f_auto,q_auto/posts/<pubid>.png with storage='cloudinary', public_id under posts/, size_bytes>0, kind='image', data_url base64 fallback present for ≤4MB images; CDN GET returns the actual PNG bytes (200). BE#2 MP4 upload → https://res.cloudinary.com/dwocjyvys/video/upload/f_auto,q_auto/... with storage='cloudinary', kind='video', duration field populated (used a real ~770KB w3schools mov_bbb.mp4 fixture cached at /tmp/iter56f_test.mp4 because the synthetic ftyp-only mp4 was rejected by Cloudinary). BE#3 scope guards: announcements scope as non-admin → 403, files scope on /uploads/media → 400, unknown MIME → 415, image >11MB → 413, video >50MB → 413 (all confirmed). BE#4 PDF upload → https://res.cloudinary.com/dwocjyvys/raw/upload/files/<pubid>.pdf with storage='cloudinary', kind='file', file_name preserved, NO f_auto/q_auto in URL (raw resources skip the transform per cloudinary_service._optimized_url), CDN GET returns bytes that start with %PDF. ZIP variant also accepted as raw. PDF >100MB → 413. BE#5 cloudinary_service.is_enabled() returns True under current /app/backend/.env config (cloud_name=dwocjyvys, key+secret loaded); disk-fallback code paths exist in /app/backend/server.py for both /uploads/media (line ~3486) and /uploads/file (line ~3545) — both branches set storage='disk' and produce backward-compatible payload shapes. BE#6 product flow: create POST /api/products with images=[cloudinary_url] returns 200 with the URL stored, GET /api/products/{id} returns {product:{images:[cloudinary_url,...]}} intact (not rewritten/stripped). BE#7 regression: 48/50 prior tests pass; the 2 failures in test_iter56d_outreach.py (test_super_admin_lists_3_templates, test_preview_handles_all_3_templates) are PRE-EXISTING — they assert 'join_the_movement' which was intentionally replaced by 'influencer_collab' in iter 56e (already documented in iteration_56e.json) — NOT a regression from iter56f. FE#1 (compose-and-render smoke) was attempted twice but blocked by the 'Welcome to your Feed' first-look modal that intercepts force-clicks; reported in action_items. Since the response shape is identical (just URL now points to https Cloudinary CDN) and SafeImage/MediaRenderer already handle absolute https URLs, the integration is logically validated by the CDN GETs passing in BE#1/BE#4.
action_items: FE#1 retry blocker: the 'Welcome to your Feed' first-look modal blocks compose interaction on a fresh login. Either add a `localStorage.setItem('feed_welcome_v1_seen','1')` bypass that the existing FE actually reads, or expose data-testid='welcome-got-it' on the dismiss button so Playwright can dismiss it deterministically. The 'Got it' button doesn't currently carry a stable selector and the modal swallowed force-clicks on create-post-button.
Pre-existing (not iter56f): /app/backend/tests/test_iter56d_outreach.py still asserts the old 'join_the_movement' template id — should be updated to 'influencer_collab' to match the iter56e change.

Cosmetic: image upload response now includes `public_id` and `storage` fields but the in-file docstring of POST /uploads/media at server.py line 3424 still says 'Streams a single image or video to disk'. Refresh the docstring to reflect the Cloudinary-first behaviour.
critical_code_review_comments: services/cloudinary_service._optimized_url uses str.replace('/upload/', '/upload/f_auto,q_auto/', 1). If the Cloudinary response ever returns a transformation already prepended (e.g. signed delivery URL with existing transforms), this would double-stack. Today Cloudinary's `secure_url` from `uploader.upload` doesn't carry transformations, so it's safe — worth a defensive check that f_auto isn't already present though.

POST /uploads/media now `await file.read()` reads the full body into memory before enforcing the size cap (3452→3454). Backend gunicorn workers will RSS-spike up to 50MB per concurrent video upload. Consider checking `file.size` or `Content-Length` first and streaming if Cloudinary supports chunked uploads (it does: `cloudinary.uploader.upload_large`).

cloudinary_service.upload_bytes uses `unique_filename=True` AND a generated `public_id`. Cloudinary actually ignores unique_filename when public_id is supplied — harmless but misleading. Safe to remove the kwarg.

Disk fallback for documents (server.py ~3546) reuses the same UPLOAD_DIR/files mount that the StaticFiles route exposes. After this migration, that disk path is essentially dead code in prod (pods get redeployed and Cloudinary handles new uploads). Consider gating it behind an explicit ENABLE_LOCAL_FALLBACK env var so accidental misconfigurations of Cloudinary aren't masked.

data_url base64 fallback is STILL emitted for images ≤4MB (server.py 3481). With Cloudinary now reliable, this doubles the response payload (≈4MB → ≈5.4MB after base64 inflation) for every image post. Either drop it once a release of confidence ships, or cap at a much smaller threshold (e.g. 256KB).

BE#6: GET /api/products/{id} returns {product, creator} envelope, but iter52 tests in test_creator_product_api.py (and iter56) appear to assume the flat shape — worth double-checking that older tests still call the right key.
